method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; seat-neutral rules in the statute's terms, exported seat questions derived from them, the filing duty as a regulative rule; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Annotated Code of Maryland, Tax-General Article, Title 10, as in effect on 1 October 2026 (mgaleg.maryland.gov, 'include enactments of the last session: Yes'), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/tax-general-title-10-subtitles-1-2-rates-and-maryland-taxable-income.txt, tax-general-title-10-subtitle-7-individual-credits.txt and tax-general-title-10-subtitle-8-returns.txt
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the statutory text is not copyrightable (see ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run mdit-cases.l4 ; l4 run mdit.l4
checks.result: 60 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings; one #TRACE of the filing duty breached as its expect comment says; mdit.l4 checks with no errors or warnings
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Full-year Maryland resident individuals, taxable years beginning in 2025 and 2026: resident (s 10-101(k)(1)(i)); Maryland adjusted gross income from federal AGI with the Social Security and Railroad Retirement subtraction (ss 10-203, 10-207(j); other additions and subtractions as totals); exemptions (s 10-211); standard and itemized deductions (ss 10-217, 10-218); Maryland taxable income (ss 10-101(i), 10-201); State rates and the 2% capital-gain addition (s 10-105(a)); county income tax at the county's flat rate (ss 10-103, 10-106); earned income credit (s 10-704), poverty-level credit (s 10-709), child tax credit (s 10-751); who must file (s 10-805), joint returns (s 10-807), the due date (s 10-820(a)) with the filing duty as a regulative rule. Out: nonresidents and part-year residents, fiduciaries, dependants claimed by others, bracket-basis counties, other credits, withholding, estimated tax, penalties. Inputs: federal figures, county rate, the Comptroller's 2026 cost-of-living adjustment, the HHS poverty guideline.
seat: the individual Maryland resident taxpayer (or married couple filing jointly)
